parole.testo: Borrowing from an Iranian language. Compare Ossetian буд (bud, “incense”) and Persian بو (bu, “smell”).

From Iranian, more specifically possibly from Alanic *ærzæ. Compare Ossetian ӕрзӕ́ (ærzǽ), Persian هزار (hezâr). The Iranian word is from Proto-Indo-Iranian *saȷ́ʰásram, from Proto-Indo-European *ǵʰéslom. The Permic languages have also borrowed this numeral from Indo-Iranian, compare Komi-Zyryan сюр

parole.testo: Uncertain. Either a native word from the fiz variant of fűz (“to string”) + -et (causative suffix) (doublet of fűzet), or from an Iranian language (compare Ossetian фидын (fidyn)) with a Hungarian (possibly instantaneous) suffix -(e)t.

parole.significato: bridge (construction or natural feature that spans a divide)
parole.testo: Possibly from an Iranian language. Compare Ossetian хид (xid).

parole.significato: flesh (the soft tissue of the body, especially muscle and fat)
parole.testo: Perhaps from an Iranian language, compare Persian گوشت (gušt), Northern Kurdish goşt.

From an Iranian language, compare Persian وام (vâm, “loan, debt”).

Borrowing from early Iranian. See Middle Persian wʾčʾl (wāzār) for more. Doublet of bazár and the stem of pazarol.

Uncertain. * Possibly from Proto-Finno-Ugric *śeppä (“skilled”) through Proto-Ugric *seppä. Hence also Proto-Samic *čeappē (“skillful”) and Proto-Finnic *seppä (“smith”). This explanation faces semantic difficulties. * Alternatively from a Turkic language, whence Chuvash шеп (šep, “beautiful”).
